summary.title: My First Language Frontend with LLVM Tutorial
summary.one_liner: A chapter-by-chapter C++ tutorial that builds the small Kaleidoscope language, from lexer and parser through LLVM IR code generation, JIT, control flow, mutable variables, object files and debug info.
keywords: how to make a compiler with llvm
takeaways: Build a small non-trivial language (Kaleidoscope) with a hand-written lexer, parser and AST in C++.
Generate LLVM IR from an AST and add JIT support with a few lines of code.
Extend the language with if/for control flow, user-defined operators and mutable variables.
Compile LLVM IR to object files and add debug information for breakpoints in the language.
The tutorial assumes C++ knowledge but no prior compiler experience, and skips some software engineering best practices for clarity.
summary.summary: This is the official LLVM tutorial for building a toy language called Kaleidoscope in C++. It is split into ten chapters that go from a lexer and recursive descent/operator precedence parser with AST, through LLVM IR code generation and JIT/optimizer support, to control flow, user-defined operators, mutable variables, object file output and debug information. The author states the code is under 1000 non-comment lines and encourages readers to copy and experiment with it. The tutorial deliberately uses globals and skips some software engineering best practices to focus on compiler techniques.
